llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Hyperliquid trading-desk helper whose network calls and financial actions match its stated purpose, with clear ticket and role limits for writes.

dimensions.detail: The skill expects Hyperliquid account/network environment variables and an existing Hyperliquid SDK exchange context from another skill; this is proportionate for exchange account management, but users should understand it can affect real trading accounts on mainnet.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains Markdown documentation, attribution, and license files only; no executable install scripts, dependency installers, hooks, services, or remote payload loaders were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions limit write actions to an Execution Trader on an approved ticket, require live position reads before closes, specify reduce-only IOC behavior, and warn against unsafe orphan-order cleanup after partial closes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, background worker, credential-store modification, local profile access, memory writing, privilege escalation, or system-level installation behavior was found.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill supports reading Hyperliquid positions, margin, open trigger orders, and margin tiers, plus high-impact write actions such as leverage changes, isolated margin updates, reduce-only closes, and cleanup of orphaned orders; these capabilities are explicitly described and fit the trading-desk purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only for users who are authorized to view and manage the referenced Hyperliquid account. Keep the default on testnet until rehearsed, and require an approved ticket before using write actions because leverage, margin, order closes, and cleanup can materially change financial exposure.
llm.findings: [E1] expected: The flagged POST requests go to Hyperliquid info API endpoints selected from mainnet or testnet and send request types plus the configured account address to retrieve account state, metadata, or open orders; this is expected for the skill's stated exchange-position purpose and does not show unrelated exfiltration.
